status: On 28 October the owner accepted soft white Watercolor edges ("yes they are!") and replied "Continue" to a report proposing the lettering and throne fixes and one rerun of this matrix for about $4.50, with an evaluation increase of about $5. Measurement only.
purpose: Rerun of the ADR 0006 launch matrix (same 33 cases, same production snapshot) after the fixes from the first run: no visible writing, nothing unseen, empty thrones, and soft Watercolor edges accepted by the check. The images shown are scored against the amended launch bar.
design: Each case is prepared once, cold, in a memory store seeded from one read-only production snapshot; a refused preparation stops that case before any image. Each stored case renders Classical, Watercolor and Icon once, with the references production would send. Every first image is checked; a faulty one gets one retry with the same request and the better image is shown, exactly as the request path does (checkAndRetry, checkScene). Cases run three at a time. The snapshot is the first run's file, unchanged, so only the pipeline differs; plans are prepared fresh because the planner version changed. Watercolor checks pass softEdges, as the request path does.

cases.expected: Light breaking over formless dark waters; no human figure for God; no text.
An aged patriarch at the end of a long life; no numerals or inscriptions.
Fire and sulfur falling on a city from a distance; no gratuitous gore; nothing modern.
Abraham with the knife raised over the altar, Isaac bound; tension without blood.
Moses' hand stretched out, a strong east wind, the sea dividing with a dry seabed; night.
Israel walking between two walls of water on dry ground; same sea, same night as the previous verse.
A pig with cloven hooves in an ancient Near Eastern setting; no text; no modern farm.
Trumpets, a shout, city walls collapsing; soldiers in Bronze Age dress.
The horror conveyed by composition and restraint, not by gore; nothing explicit.
Three generations of a family line in Bethlehem; no name labels.
A young shepherd's sling stone striking a giant warrior's forehead; valley battlefield.
Youths mocking a bald prophet on the road up to Bethel; the bears not yet shown as a bloodbath.
A storm-voice over cosmic foundations being laid; Job small before it; no literal bearded deity.
Green pastures and still waters with sheep and a shepherd; calm.
Exiles weeping by Babylon's rivers with harps hung on willows.
A rose of Sharon and a lily of the valleys; tasteful, no nudity.
Six-winged seraphim above a throne, faces and feet covered; temple smoke.
Wolf and lamb, leopard and kid, calf and lion together, a little child leading them.
A prophet speaking over a valley of dry bones; eerie but not horror.
Daniel unharmed among lions in a den, an angelic presence; dawn light from above.
A throne of flames with burning wheels, white garments, hair like wool; visionary, not a portrait.
A great fish swallowing Jonah in a stormy sea.
A scroll or family line from Abraham through David to Jesus, shown without legible writing.
Peter stepping out of the boat onto the water toward Jesus at night in a storm.
Peter throwing himself into the sea from the boat at dawn, the same fisherman as on the Galilee storm.
Jesus standing in a boat rebuking wind and waves, the sea suddenly calm.
A father running to embrace a ragged returning son on the road.
Jesus calling at a tomb's mouth as a wrapped figure emerges; mourners.
A blinding light from heaven around a traveler on the Damascus road.
An abstract-leaning but era-true image of providence; no text of the verse.
Soldiers casting lots for garments beneath the cross; the crucifixion treated seriously, no gratuitous gore.
A sea of glass before the throne and four living creatures full of eyes.
A new heaven and new earth, the sea gone; luminous, vast.

scoring.method: As in the first run, with batches of about 16 images per scorer (eight batches, two independent scorers each), saved as they go. SCORING.md adds that a soft Watercolor fade to white is part of the style and that halo, title-board and corner marks count as lettering. The operator adjudicates disagreements by viewing the images, with the first run's written rules, and commits before unblinding. Not human acceptance.
scoring.launchBar: ADR 0006 as amended on 28 October, on the images shown: at least 75% acceptable overall and at least 65% in each style; a no-form subject drawn as a figure in at most 1 in 20 shown images of cases whose plan selects one. Watercolor margins are reported, not gated. Owner sign-off on the contact sheet follows separately.
scoring.alsoReported: First-attempt quality without the check, the retry rate, the check's agreement with the adjudicated labels on first attempts (new evidence for the figure question), refusals, latency per sample and cost. Comparison with the first run per case and cause.

knownLimitation: One image per case and style; model scorers can miss subtle figures or edges. Thirty-three chosen cases weight dramatic and theophany scenes more than a random draw would. The fixes were chosen after seeing the first run's images, so this rerun of the same cases favours them; a random-verse draw would be independent.
